messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT OPENED • high throttle rate on inference-pool-us-east-2 at 2025-06-03T17:13:03Z — paging oncall (severity: P1) :rotating_light:

maria: oncall here, seeing alerts. what's the current customer impact?

lucy: hitting 15-20% throttle events across gpu-pool-04, tokens/sec spiked from 120k -> 420k in last 5m. queue depth climbed from ~30 to ~350 for short requests. A few customer requests returned 429s.

jon: bad timing — rolling canary pushed a new batching tweak ~16:45. telemetry shows continuous batching being more aggressive for short sequences (batch window 30ms -> 80ms). Likely increased in-flight requests and pushed queue length.

maria: ok, immediate mitigation options?

jon: stepping through: 1) roll back canary to previous batching config (safe) 2) temporarily bump autoscale min nodes for that pool + enable burst capacity 3) suppress noisy queue-depth alert while we stabilize

lucy: doing #2 now: `infra-cli scale --pool gpu-pool-04 --min-instances 20` (was 6) — expecting new instances to join in ~3m.

sre-oncall: +1 to rollback if quick. If rollback not instant, we should patch routing to send traffic to alternate model variant to avoid degrading customer response.

maria: jon, can you roll back canary?

jon: initiating rollback: `deployctl rollback canary inference/batching-config@canary-2025-06-03` — kicking off now.

incident-bot: Deploy rollback job started (job-id: rbk-7753).

lucy: autoscale up confirmed, new instances healthy in 180s. throttle rate dropping but queue depth still noisy (oscillating).

product-ops: we're seeing client 842 and 1103 report intermittent 429s. Triage notes for CS: brief impact window ~16:40-17:10, most retries succeeded.

maria: good. I'm going to mute the queue-depth alert for this pool for 15m to reduce noise while we watch. Setting a short-term suppression rather than deleting rule.

jon: rollback completed and verified — batch-window reverted. Metrics show tokens/sec back down to ~140k and throttle events trending to baseline.

lucy: confirmed. re-enabling normal routing. customer 842 confirms latencies returned to normal.

maria: incident -> containment achieved. moving to post-incident tuning discussion in-thread.

jon: quick notes on root cause: aggressive batching tweak increased average in-flight latency for short-seq workloads, which compounded with autoscale cooldown settings (cooldown=5m) and min-instances low. Two levers failed to absorb spike: slow scale-up reaction and alerting that fired too early.

maria: action items proposal: (A) alert tuning: make queue-depth alert require sustained 3m median > threshold + throttle_count > X, (B) add tokens/sec per-instance metric to dashboard and alert, (C) quick dashboard panels to show in-flight_batch_window vs requests_per_batch, (D) autoscale policy tweak: lower scale cooldown to 90s for this pool and add rapid-burst policy when tokens/sec surge > 200k.

lucy: agree. current queue-depth alert is a single instantaneous value (> 100). That creates noise on transient spikes. We should change it to evaluate: `moving_avg(queue_depth, 3m, median) > 80 AND rate(throttle_events[3m]) > 5`

jon: here's a draft Grafana/Prometheus alert snippet — please copy/paste and sanity-check before I file a PR: ```yaml
alert: HighQueueAndThrottle
expr: avg_over_time(queue_depth{pool=\"gpu-pool-04\"}[3m]) > 80 and increase(throttle_events_total{pool=\"gpu-pool-04\"}[3m]) > 5
for: 2m
labels:
  severity: page
annotations:
  summary: "Sustained queue depth + throttle spike in gpu-pool-04"
  runbook: "https://redwood.internal/runbooks/autoscale-throttle"
```

maria: looks good. let's change `for` to 5m to avoid paging on short-lived bursts, and evaluate with median rather than avg. The intent is avoid waking ppl for 2-min blips.

lucy: +1. Also propose creating a derived metric `tokens_per_instance = tokens/sec / instance_count` and alert if `tokens_per_instance > 10000` sustained 3m. That catches hot machines rather than global spikes.

product-ops: can we add a customer-impact tag to alerts (e.g., alerts that correlate with 429s count) so CS can prioritize?

jon: we can. plan: add `alert_labels: {customer_impact: true}` when `increase(429_responses_total[5m]) > 0`. Will need to instrument rule to evaluate both signals.

maria: follow-up assignments: jon -> PR for alert rule changes + add tokens_per_instance metric (due EOD), lucy -> dashboard panels + grafana dash with batch-window vs request/batch (due tomorrow), maria -> autoscale policy change + test in staging (due tomorrow). product-ops -> create CS note template for impacted clients (low-boiling) and tag alerts (due EOD).

sre-oncall: also recommend we add a synthetic canary test that runs a high short-seq traffic profile after any batching-config deploy — fails should block canary promotion.

maria: agreed, add to postmortem. I'll kick off a short write-up and link to runbook.

jon: one more small tweak to alerting: add a suppression window tied to deploy events — if a deploy is in progress, suppress immediate pages for 10m unless 429s are observed. Helps avoid noisy alerts during known changes.

lucy: note — make sure deploy suppression doesn't mute global/API-level paging. Only per-pool deploy suppression.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED • severity downgraded to P3 at 2025-06-03T17:45:10Z — containment confirmed.

maria: handing off to night shift: @sre-oncall you're up for monitoring the follow-ups. If anything weird pops up, escalate to me.

sre-oncall: ack. will monitor tokens_per_instance and throttle_events dashboards for 3 hours.

product-ops: CS notified affected customers with the template. Will update if any follow-up requests.

maria: closing thread for real after I file the postmortem. Thanks all. :heart:
